messages.body_plain:
On Feb 1, 2009, at 12:49 , Russ Lenth wrote:

> I wonder who can tell me what's going wrong here (see session appended
> below my signature).  These examples are straight from the man page  
> for
> .jcall().  The first one at least ensures me that I can talk to Java,
> sometimes.  But the next one requires AWT, nd that's the problem.  I
> looked all over my system (with no success) for Init.plist files that
> might have "StartOnFirstThread" in them.  Is there some argument I  
> need
> to supply in, say, the .jinit() call?
>

No, Leopard simply does not support AWT in R (more precisely Apple has  
removed support for Java in single-threaded applications from 10.5).  
You have to use JGR in order to use AWT in R.

Cheers,
Simon

> Hi there!

> Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 1.6.0_07-b06-57, mixed mode)

Note that Apple's J2SE 1.6 is 64-bit Intel *only*, so you cannot use  
it with regular 32-bit R. Switch back to J2SE 1.5 if in doubt or use  
64-bit R (from http://r.research.att.com/ ) *and* either set  
FORCE_NATIVE=yes or use the latest 0.6-2 branch snapshot (see  
configure message about the architectures supported and the  
FORCE_NATIVE flag).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Passing R objects between JRI/Java classes
messages.subject_clean: Passing R objects between JRI/Java classes
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Is there a way to pass R objects, such as hclust objects between
JRI/Java classes. 
So, say for example I have a class called getUPGMA() which produces a
hclust object like so:

REXP rexp = re.eval ("dist <- hclust (upgma_matrix, method =
"average")");

...and I want to pass 'dist', as an hclust object to a class called
plotDendrogram(). What's the best way?

Currently, the only way I can see is by assigning dist to a REXP object
in getUPGMA, passing it to the class plotDendrogram() and then getting
the raw content with rexp.getContent(). The problem here is that if I
want to create something like a dendrogram using plot(dist), then dist
has to be an hclust object. What, if any, is the best way to pass R
objects between Java classes?
For example, is there anyway of 're-forming' an hclust object from the
rexp.getContent() method, or am I barking up the wrong tree here? 

Many thanks,
Graham Etherington

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
 
Yesterday I installed the latest JGR from CRAN for R 2.8.1, and the launcher from http://jgr.markushelbig.org/Download.html
 
I had package rJava 0.6-0 already installed and working correctly. It was used by several applications like StatET and Biocep. I'm using Windows XP Pro, R 2.8.1, and Java 1.6. Session info below.
 
Nevertheless, after installing JGR, rJava no longer loads from normal R sessions:
 
> library(rJava)
Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) : 
  unable to load shared library 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-28~1.1/library/rJava/libs/rJava.dll':
  LoadLibrary failure:  The specified module could not be found.

Error : .onLoad failed in 'loadNamespace' for 'rJava'
Error: package/namespace load failed for 'rJava'

This is strange, as the "rJava.dll" is available where it is searched.
 
All other applications using rJava no longer work, but JGR loads rJava and works correctly when invoked from "jgr.exe".
 
What change may have produced this effect? I've removed and reinstalled the rJava package, without any success. Any help really appreciated. 
 
Best,
 
Enrique
